claim: A delay-time byte does not scale a time and does not run a formula. It indexes a ladder of round decimal milliseconds whose step changes a few times over the byte, and every entry is then cut back to a whole step of a clock running at 32000 Hz -- which is what a delay addressed as a sample count does to a time written in milliseconds. The range the page prints picks which ladder. On 0 - 500m the step is a tenth of a millisecond to setting fifty, then a half to sixty, then one to ninety, then ten to a hundred and sixteen, then twenty to a hundred and twenty-six; on 0 - 100m it is the same tenth to fifty and half to sixty, then one to a hundred, then two to a hundred and twenty-five; on 200m - 990m/1sec the byte starts at two hundred milliseconds and steps five to setting seventy, then ten to a hundred and fifteen, where it reaches one second; on 0m - 635m the step never changes at all -- five milliseconds from the first setting to the last; and 0m - 500m, which the page spells with an m the other five-hundred range does not have, is that range's ladder entry for entry. Four of the five reach the printed end before the byte ends and repeat it at every setting above, and the fifth reaches it at its last setting, so where a ladder stops is read off the record in both directions. The cut is not a detail of the ladder: it is what the settings at the short end actually return, and it is what decides which settings the reading brings back a tall peak for. It is also why two of the five ranges say nothing about the clock -- every entry on them is five milliseconds or more, which is already a whole step of it, so there is no setting at which the two readings differ.
why_not_named: The ladder is the claim and it is written out. A name for it would be a name for a table somebody laid out by hand, and there is nothing to call it but the numbers.

document_rows.read_as: The printed range is taken to say what the byte reaches at its ends and nothing about what it does between them. That it picks the table is no longer only an arrangement carried from a neighbouring class: the two types 0 - 500m is printed against return the same quefrency at every setting asked of both, including the two where a whole sample and a round millisecond disagree -- and there both return the same lowered peak, which is the grid showing rather than the times agreeing. The shorter range then turns out to be a different ladder and not this one stopped early, which is the other half of the same reading: the range does not merely fail to be ignored, it selects. The fourth row is also the first read on a parameter number other than one, and its range is a fourth ladder: so what picks the table is the printed range and not the position the parameter sits at. The fifth row settles what keying by a printed string does with the page's own typography. Two of these ranges are five hundred milliseconds spelled two ways -- one carries an m on the lower end and the other does not -- which makes them different keys and could have made them different tables. Read at every setting on two types they are one table, so the m is typesetting. They are kept as two keys rather than merged, because what was measured is that two spellings agree and a merge would publish that as a string somebody normalised.

two_spellings_of_one_range.why: No setting differs by as much as two of the capture's own quefrencies, and the ones that differ by one go both ways in roughly equal numbers. A table read one bin high here and one bin low there is one table read twice; a different table would not be able to stay inside a bin for a hundred and twenty-eight settings, and a rig reading one type long would not change sign.

era_priors.claim: A delay line is addressed as a count of samples, so the times a byte selects are whole samples of whatever the part clocks at and not the round milliseconds a page prints.
era_priors.why: A delay is a read pointer some distance behind a write pointer in a buffer, and that distance is an integer. Nothing in the era interpolates between two samples of a delay line to reach a printed millisecond; it would cost a multiply per sample to make a number on a page true.
era_priors.would_be_wrong_if: The times had come back on round milliseconds at the settings where a whole sample and a round millisecond disagree. 120 settings across the five ranges are such settings, and every one of them came back on the sample. They are all on the two ranges whose step falls under a millisecond: the other two never step finer than five milliseconds, which is a hundred and sixty whole steps of the clock, so neither has such a setting and neither is evidence here.

adds: The records say where the copy came back at each of the byte's hundred and twenty-eight settings, and how far each peak stood over the take's own roughness. What is read out of them here is that the times lie on a ladder of round steps, that the ladder is cut to a sample grid, which grid, and that the printed range picks which ladder. The grid does not come from the times at all: it comes from the peak heights, which no table of times can arrange, and it is arrived at separately on each of the two types read at every setting.
a_prediction_that_was_made_first: The 0 - 100m ladder was written down and committed before the sweep that reads it, from the four settings the two ranges had already been seen to share and two further ones. It got the shape right and the breakpoint wrong: the prediction was a two-millisecond step from setting a hundred and four, and the unit changes step at a hundred. The error was in forcing the printed end onto the byte's last setting, when the longer range was already saturating two settings early and that had not been carried over. What survives is the part worth carrying to the four ranges still unread -- the step sizes transfer and the breakpoints do not, so a breakpoint is measured rather than solved for.

alternatives.reading: The ladder is in round milliseconds and the unit reaches them, so the 120 settings that came back short are the reading being short rather than the unit.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: The heights of the peaks. They split each byte's settings in two, and which side a setting falls on is predicted with nothing fitted by whether its time is a whole step of a clock at 32000 Hz. This candidate has no account of the split at all, and its own residual is further out than one setting's resolution at the shortest delay the slot makes -- on each of the records whose ladder steps finer than a whole step of the clock.

separated_by.observable: The time at the settings where a whole sample and a round millisecond disagree, and the height of the peak there.

predicts.a-ladder-cut-to-whole-samples: no setting further out than that setting alone could be, on any of the five records
predicts.a-ladder-of-round-milliseconds: a setting further out than it could be on each record whose ladder steps finer than the clock, and no account of the heights at all

separated_by.sensitivity_here: The settings a rate puts on the capture's own grid stand 2.522 spreads of the heights over the settings it does not, at 32000 Hz, against 1.608 for the next rate that predicts anything at all. A setting taken again moved 0.78 where the spread is 8.512. The other bytes read at every setting, on other types and other printed ranges, each name the same rate on their own: 01-40 puts 32000 Hz at 1.991 spreads against 1.519 for the next rate; 01-57 puts 32000 Hz at 2.411 spreads against 1.533 for the next rate.

alternatives.reading: The byte scales a time rather than indexing one -- a straight line or a run of equal ratios between the printed ends.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: The readings themselves, by whole octaves, on four of the five ranges. A straight line through the ends of 0 - 500m puts nothing under four milliseconds and the slot reaches a twelfth of one; a run of equal ratios reaches both ends and is wrong by more than an octave over most of what lies between, on every range including the one the line is right on.
alternatives.where_it_is_not_separated: On 0m - 635m the straight line is the reading, exactly. That range's ladder has one segment -- five milliseconds a setting from the first to the last, reaching the printed end at setting a hundred and twenty-seven -- so a line through the printed ends and the ladder predict the same time at every one of its settings, and both come back at no setting over its own floor with a worst residual of zero. That range separates the two candidates by nothing at all, and it is stated rather than absorbed into a total because a total would show it as the line losing by a hundred and thirty settings it did not lose. What the line is beaten by is the other three ranges, where the step changes and a line cannot. This is also why the line was given each page's printed bottom and no shade above it: a candidate handed a bottom it did not ask for would have failed here by the handicap rather than by the times, and the range that shows the claim is a shape read off the unit would have been the range that hid it.

separated_by.observable: The time at every setting between the two ends.
separated_by.sensitivity_here: The run resolved a setting taken four times onto one quefrency. The run of equal ratios is wrong by whole octaves over most of every byte read. The straight line is wrong by whole octaves over most of four of the five, and right at every setting of the fifth.

refuted_by: A reading at any setting of any of these slots that is not its range's ladder entry for it, by more than that setting's own resolution. Or a slot on another type one of these ranges is printed against whose ladder has different steps, which would make the printed range the wrong thing to index by. Or the same sweep on a unit whose delay is not clocked at 32000 Hz coming back with the heights split the same way, which would mean the split is not the grid.

compared_against.generated_from: Every record this class has, on every printed range it has one for. Five of the six are read at every setting the byte has, on five types and five ranges; the sixth is read at seven settings spanning three orders of magnitude and is there to answer whether two types printing one range share a ladder. Three of the swept bytes are the parameter the page numbers one and one is the parameter it numbers seventeen, which is the last stage of a chain of four.
compared_against.why_not_a_filter: There is nothing to filter. The set is every record this class has, and each is scored against the table its own printed range picks.

stimulus: channel 2, program 126, note 60, velocity 100, held 8.0 s, captured 9.0 s, 40 12 31 = 0
domain.outside: How much of the output the returned copy is, which a cepstral peak does not weigh. What the other delay byte of a type does, which was parked for the whole run and not swept. Whether the ladder is the same on the rest of the class: the 5 ranges read here cover 54 of the class's 55 rows, and one slot of each range was read, so the claim is that the range picks the table and not that the other 1 rows were asked.

residual.why: The median is zero: the ladder returns the reading's own value at 552 of the 660 settings scored across the 6 records, and the rest are inside half a quefrency. The worst is at setting one, which is the shortest delay these slots make and the one the reading resolves worst -- half a quefrency is a fifth of an octave there. It is inside that setting's own floor. The swing above is reported against a single floor over the whole byte and it is the wrong yardstick here for the same reason: a byte covering three orders of magnitude has no one floor, which is why every setting is also counted against its own.

gross.why: The median residual over the span the byte commands. A rejection bound and not a target: below it the residual is reported and never optimised, because no candidate is decided by it.

qualitative.property: longer or shorter than the shortest setting the record admits
qualitative.why: Every setting above the shortest the record admits is longer than it, in the unit and in the model alike. The byte is monotonic and so is the ladder.

power.why: The strongest competing candidate is the same ladder without the cut, and it is not beaten on the residual alone -- it is contradicted by a reading it cannot produce. The heights of the peaks split the settings in two, and which side a setting falls on is predicted with nothing fitted by whether its time is a whole step of the clock. A table of times has no way to reach the height of a cepstral peak. The three bytes this can be read off are on three types and three printed ranges, and the scan names the same rate on each of them separately.
power.why_not_every_record: Two of the five bytes read at every setting cannot name a rate and are not asked to. The scan works by which settings land on a quefrency the capture has and which fall between two, so a ladder whose every entry is already a whole step of the clock predicts every setting tall -- a prediction that cannot come out wrong. Both ranges that never step finer than five milliseconds are of that kind. Including them would add two records that agree with every rate equally.

breakdown.why: How many settings are further out than that setting alone could be, and by how much. The floors above are each one number over the whole byte, and this byte covers three orders of magnitude: half a quefrency is a fifth of an octave at its shortest setting and a ten-thousandth of one at its longest. A single floor is therefore far over the reading at one end and far under it at the other, so a candidate wrong where the reading is coarse passes it and a candidate right everywhere can fail it. This counts each setting against its own. It is reported beside the swing and does not replace it: the swing asks whether the residual leans, which is a different question from whether any one reading disagrees. One of the terms in it is not a quantisation at all: a delay is counted in the unit's clock and read in the one the take was captured on, so the whole reading is scaled by whatever those two sit apart, which is nothing at a tenth of a millisecond and more than a quefrency at a second. It is the same number of octaves everywhere and it is taken from the unit's own records, so a floor that left it out would be tighter than the rig at the long end and nowhere else.

reproduces.why_the_decoy_is_not_ranked: Its entries are the readings. It reproduces the record because it is the record, its residual is the reading's own rounding, and it could not have come out wrong. It is written and named so that the ranking has to beat it rather than quietly not contain it.

what_this_does_not_close.what: The printed ranges this class has rows on and no reading of: 5 - 500m.
what_this_does_not_close.why: 5 of the class's 6 printed ranges were read at every setting, covering 54 of its 55 rows. The other 1 rows carry one of the 1 ranges named above, and nothing here reaches them. What the five that were read establish is that a range is not another range stopped early, and that they do not even share a shape: two of them share their first two steps exactly and then part, one begins at two hundred milliseconds rather than nothing, and one never changes step at all. So an unread range's ladder cannot be derived from these -- the step sizes are a reasonable expectation, the breakpoints are not, and how many breakpoints there are is not either.
what_this_does_not_close.what_would_close_it: The same sweep on one slot of each range, at every setting. Two runs of about half an hour each -- one of the remaining ranges holds a single row and it is the one this reading cannot reach.

what_this_does_not_close.what: The gate time printed 5 - 500m, which is one row of this class.
what_this_does_not_close.why: Its range puts it here and its quantity is not a delay. It is how long a gate stays open over a reverb, and nothing in that output is a copy of anything -- so there is no peak for this reading to place, whatever the byte does. A run of it would return the roughness at every setting and the record would say so, which is a cost with no answer at the end of it.
what_this_does_not_close.what_would_close_it: An envelope read rather than a cepstral one: how long the output stays up after the note stops, at each setting. That is the decay stage's question and it has no delay-time record to write into.

what_this_does_not_close.what: Setting zero, on the three ranges whose page begins at zero.
what_this_does_not_close.why: Four of the five printed ranges begin at zero and all four ladders say no delay at all there, so there is no ratio to be wrong by and the comparison cannot be made. The fourth begins at two hundred milliseconds and has no such setting. The reading admitted a peak at the bottom of its own search on each of the other records, but the neighbours do not sit at three and five times it the way a copy's do, so what it found is most likely the shape of the source and not a delay.
what_this_does_not_close.what_would_close_it: A stimulus whose own log spectrum is flatter at the bottom of the search, or a longer frame, so that the residue the subtraction leaves there falls under the bar.

what_this_does_not_close.what: Any delay this stimulus's own repeat could be mistaken for, which on this note is around nine hundred and fifty-one milliseconds.
what_this_does_not_close.why: The take with the part routed past the effect, read against another of itself, leaves a peak there on every run that searches far enough to meet it and on every one that was re-read out to it -- five types, five sweeps, five days, and one of them is not even a delay on its own but the last stage of a chain of four. It is the stimulus and not any effect: the note is a held sample and a sample that loops puts a copy of itself in the output at its loop length, which is the one thing this reading cannot tell from a delay. Only the longest range searches far enough to meet it; the other four stop well below, and their nulls are clean inside the search each was published with. On the range that does, the ladder walks straight through without sticking -- setting a hundred and ten reads nine hundred and fifty and not nine hundred and fifty-one, fifty quefrencies away -- and every setting stands three to nine times what the stimulus's own peak stands. So the readings are admitted and the bound is stated rather than the run being thrown away.
what_this_does_not_close.what_would_close_it: The same sweep on a stimulus with no loop in it at this length -- a percussive note, or one of the unit's shorter samples -- which would move the peak rather than remove it, and two stimuli whose loops differ would separate the delay from the source at every setting.

what_this_does_not_close.what: Where inside the two clocks' own bound this rig sat during these runs.
what_this_does_not_close.why: A delay is counted in the unit's clock and read in the interface's, so every reading is scaled by whatever those two sit apart. Read off the peak's own vertex rather than the bin it falls in, the runs that have a setting fine enough to show it come back between nine and seventeen parts per million long, which sits inside the bound this archive already published for the two clocks and is why the floor allows for it. Which figure it was on any one take is not known and is not asked: it is nothing at a tenth of a millisecond and a little over one quefrency at a second, so it changes no reading and only the floor the longest range is judged against.
what_this_does_not_close.what_would_close_it: Clocking the interface from the unit, which this unit does not offer, or measuring the offset on each take against something of known length in it. Neither is worth a run: the term is already bounded and the bound is under one entry of every ladder here.

what_this_does_not_close.what: Whether the clock is the whole unit's or this effect's.
what_this_does_not_close.why: The heights say the delay counts in steps of a clock at 32000 Hz. They say nothing about what else runs on it.
what_this_does_not_close.what_would_close_it: The same reading on a type whose stage is not a delay line -- a rate, a band edge -- landing on the same grid.

a_note_on_what_was_left_out: Nothing was left out by any record's own controls: every setting asked stood over the bar on all six records. One setting per record beginning at zero is left out of the comparison and not of the record, because a residual is a ratio and the winning candidate puts no time on one side of it there. Four runs' own nulls -- one take with the effect out read against another, which is this reading with the delay taken out of it -- came back under the bar, so the settings that did stand over it could have failed to. The longest range's null did not: it stands at thirteen times the roughness, at the stimulus's own repeat. That is named above rather than quietly passed, and what admits the run is that its weakest setting stands three times higher again and lands fifty quefrencies away.

a_printing_read_after_this_was_made.what_it_is: The table the manual prints for the effect parameters it does not store in the quantity they are set in: fourteen columns, each giving a setting at every one of the byte's 128 values. It is cited by column number because that is what the effect list prints beside such a parameter, and because the three places the manual names these quantities spell some of the names differently.
a_printing_read_after_this_was_made.why_it_is_held_out: It was unread when this claim was made, not withheld. The manual had been read for its parameter address map and for nothing else, and these two pages were among the two hundred and fifty that nobody had looked at.
a_printing_read_after_this_was_made.why_it_is_not_in_rests_on: A claim resting on a printed page is a different claim from one resting on readings, and it can fail in a different way. Moving this under `rests_on` would also spend the one thing the comparison is worth, which is that the page was not an input.
a_printing_read_after_this_was_made.what_it_cannot_do: A page is not a reading and cannot refute a claim about a unit. What an agreement says is that the list in the part is the list the publisher documented, which is a second origin for the same numbers and not a second measurement of them. What a disagreement says is that one of the two is wrong about this unit, and which one is a question for the unit.
a_printing_read_after_this_was_made.the_page_prints_the_ladder_and_not_the_c: The page gives round decimal milliseconds and the claim gives whole steps of a clock, so the two are compared with the cut applied to the page: a printed tenth of a millisecond is 3.2 steps at 32000 Hz and the claim says the part returns 3. That is the whole of the transform, it has no fitted number in it, and it is applied to the page rather than undone on the claim so that nothing is rounded twice.
a_printing_read_after_this_was_made.what_it_settles: Every ladder the claim names is a column of this grid, at every setting the page states a value for, once cut. The page and the readings were in a position to disagree at each of five step changes and at five different ends, and they do not disagree anywhere. The two halves of the claim come from different places and neither could have produced the other: the ladder is what the publisher wrote down, and the cut is the only part that is about the hardware -- which is why this agreement is evidence for a clock at 32000 Hz and not for the ladder.

a_ladder_the_page_prints_and_this_claim_.why: Nothing measured here was on it. The grid's index names one effect type under it, so it is one type's worth of work rather than a hole across the class -- and until the effect list is read, which type that is, is a number in an index with no two bytes beside it.
a_ladder_the_page_prints_and_this_claim_.what_would_close_it: The efx-time stage on the one type the index names, at the settings where this column's step changes. It bends at a different setting from every ladder already read, so a run that found the bend where the page puts it could not have found it by carrying anything over from those.
